# Building a fabric {#sec-building}

[Back to dashboard](../lab-dashboard.html)

Our example fabric has two spine switches, two leaf switches and two Linux
hosts. Each leaf connects to both spines; each host connects to one leaf.

## Device roles {#sec-device-roles}

| Role | Nodes | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Spine | spine-1, spine-2 | Carry routed traffic between leaves |
| Leaf | leaf-1, leaf-2 | Attach hosts and terminate VXLAN tunnels |
| Host | host-1, host-2 | Send traffic through the fabric |

: Example inventory. {#tbl-inventory}

## Underlay links {#sec-underlay}

The underlay provides IP reachability between the switches. The overlay carries
tenant traffic using EVPN and VXLAN. Verify the underlay before troubleshooting
overlay routes.

::: {.callout-tip}
Give each point-to-point link its own subnet and keep interface descriptions
consistent at both ends. This makes a failed adjacency easier to trace.
:::

## Example topology fragment

```yaml
# Displayed as text; this example never starts containers.
name: preview-fabric
topology:
  nodes:
    spine-1:
      kind: ceos
    leaf-1:
      kind: ceos
  links:
    - endpoints: ["spine-1:eth1", "leaf-1:eth1"]
```

Continue with the checks in @sec-checking. The next chapter links back to
@tbl-inventory and @sec-underlay to exercise cross-file references.
